description:
Goal
A callable surface that publishes a transport boundary names a runtime dispatch site, so it must be GROUND. Stop type-variable-bearing (polymorphic template) surfaces from leaking into runtime facts and minting phantom boundaries.

Problem
When a first-class callable escapes through a generic parameter slot AND a concrete call instantiates it (e.g. the Enum.with_index mapper threading through the generic recursive with_index_list/3), analysis collects both the polymorphic template surfaces (e.g. (a0,a0), (a0,a1)) and the grounded sibling ((binary,int)). The templates are not distinct runtime dispatch sites -- the grounded sibling is what the runtime invokes -- but they were carried into CallableFlowFact.first_class_surfaces and into callable demand .resolved sets, then transport minted one boundary per surface. Result: a single boxed value's publication position owns multiple boundaries, which native correctly rejects:
  transport position ExecutableInput{...} is published by multiple callable boundaries [BoundaryId(1), BoundaryId(2)]

The pre-existing reconciliation (retain_most_specific_surfaces + fold_direct_surfaces_into_first_class_publication + callable_surface_subsumes) reimplemented subsumption with a per-position is_subtype || key_var_count>0 check that mishandles a variable recurring across positions (treats the two a0 in (a0,a0) independently), so it failed to collapse the templates and even fanned a single template out into several surfaces.

Fix (landed)
- Types calculator owns the relationship fact: new memoized key_list_subsumes (consistent-Sigma subsumption built on key_subsumes_with) + key_has_vars. A recurring template var now binds once and must agree across positions.
- One shared semantic::ground_dispatch_surfaces helper resolves each surface to ground dispatch shapes: ground surfaces kept; templates replaced by the ground surfaces that instantiate them; a genuinely-polymorphic escape with no ground sibling keeps its template.
- Enforced at the demand->representation seam: callable_flows first-class surfaces grounded at construction; ExecutableRuntimeDemand.ground_callable_surfaces seals all callable axes at demand finalization; boundary_runtime_demand grounds type-derived surfaces.
- Deleted retain_most_specific_surfaces, fold_direct_surfaces_into_first_class_publication, callable_surface_subsumes.

Proof
- Types unit tests (key_list_subsumes/key_has_vars) and semantic ground_dispatch_surfaces unit tests.
- The with_index repro no longer produces the multi-boundary publication conflict; full lib suite green (only the end-to-end with_index drive test still ignored, blocked on fz-hwn.22).

Scope note
This fixes the surface/boundary leak only. The end-to-end with_index test re-enablement is blocked on fz-hwn.22 (first-class callable captured by a non-tail-recursive continuation gets a 0-lane contract shape), a separate transport-representation bug this fix unmasked.
title: Ground first-class callable publication surfaces (phantom polymorphic surface leak)
